title: Gigging with Armstrong and Alberta Hunter; Racehorse Williams and King Jones
summary: He made small gigs with Louis and Alberta Hunter, and describes dancer Racehorse Williams and the self-styled British emcee King Jones at the Dreamland.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What was Lou Armstrong doing then?
Lou was gigging, she was gigging around. Playing dances -- I mean little places, I made quite a few gigs with Lou Armstrong.
And Alberta Hunter did you play with her?
Yes, yes. And Racehorse Williams, I guess you never heard of Racehorse Williams?
Racehorse Williams was a real thin girl, she was one of the greatest dancers in Chicago, at that time.

She had a -- she was real thin, but had a very pretty figure and fast as a racehorse, she'd get on the floor and she could twist and turn and she tore up everything, she was very famous then in Chicago at that time. And she and King Jones, it was King Jones, did you ever hear of King Jones?

King Jones was a guy that went around all the clubs, from club to club, and he wore long full -- what do you call it -- full dress tail and his white tie and he would make announcements and would introduce all the acts in all the clubs and he tried to be British, you know?
And he was a very comical person. He was at the Dreamland at the time, and Racehorse Williams, it was the only show that they had.
